title: South Downs Way 100 2027 — official race page
claims: The SDW100 is a 100 mile non-stop foot race taking in the entire South Downs Way National Trail, from just outside Winchester east to Eastbourne; the page calls it the 16th Annual and says the race is part of the World Trail Majors Series.

The vital-stats panel gives 100 mi / 161 km, 12,700 ft / 3,800 m of elevation, a 30 hour cut-off, an entry fee of £225, the date 12 Jun 2027 05:30, 600 starters, 12 aid stations, 15% road / 85% trail, an average temperature of 15 C, average rainfall of 52 mm and average humidity of 60%.
The page lists course records of David Green (M) 13:27:13 in 2026 and Sarah Webster (F) 14:27:34 in 2026.

Entries for 2027 open at 1900 on Sunday 19 July 2026 on a first come, first served basis; the fee is £225 (£227 unaffiliated); 100 free places go to volunteers; elite applicants are guided by an ITRA Index of 750+ for men and 600+ for women.
Qualification is a minimum 50 mile distance race completed within 15 hours between 1 January 2020 and race day.
The race is held under a full UK Athletics Permit granted through the TRA, with the permit number still to be confirmed (TBC).
The race starts in two waves on Saturday 12 June 2027, Wave 1 at 0530 and Wave 2 at 0630, with waves set by estimated finish time and no changes once published about three weeks before the event.
Registration and the start are at Matterley Bowl; the finish is at Eastbourne Sports Club Athletics Track, where runners complete a lap of the track.
Entry includes 12 fully stocked aid stations, a marked course, overnight camping at the start line, full medical support, live tracking, finish-line hot food and a finishers buckle.

The Route section says the race begins with a 4 mile loop through Matterley Estate before joining the South Downs Way as it passes through the farm, and that the final 96 miles remain identical to previous years. The same page says the first 5 miles around Matterley Estate are entirely private land and must not be recce'd.

All aid stations from Houghton onwards have hot drinks including tea and coffee; hot food is available at Washington and the finish line, and soup or other hot food is available at some aid stations across the second half of the course.
